title: Practice 4: Running, swimming, climbing, crawling, dragging

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Кошка ___ (гнаться — to drive, chase (oneself)) за мышью.
exercises.why: **гонится** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **гнаться** (to chase, to pursue [with за (za, + accusative) ‘someone’]) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **гоняться** for many directions. present: я гоню́сь · ты го́нишься · он го́нится · мы го́нимся · вы го́нитесь · они го́нятся. — Wiktionary, «гнаться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Я попросил его не ___ (гнать — to drive, chase, one way).
exercises.why: **гнать** (the infinitive) (to drive (to forcibly cause someone or something to move)) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **гонять** for many directions. — Wiktionary, «гнать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I asked him not to drive fast.
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Мальчик ___ (гнать — to drive, chase, one way) стадо овец.
exercises.why: **гнал** is the past tense (masculine) of **гнать** (to drive (to forcibly cause someone or something to move)) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **гонять** for many directions. past: он гна́л · она гнала́ · оно гна́ло · они гна́ли. — Wiktionary, «гнать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: A boy was driving a flock of sheep.
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Не ___ (гнать — to drive, chase, one way) меня как собаку.
exercises.why: **гони** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **гнать** (to drive (to forcibly cause someone or something to move)) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **гонять** for many directions. imperative: гони́ · гони́те. — Wiktionary, «гнать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Don't shoo me as though I were a dog.
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Я никогда не ___ (кататься — to roll (oneself)) на скейте.
exercises.why: **катался** is the past tense (masculine) of **кататься** (to ride in a vehicle) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **катиться** for one direction. past: он ката́лся · она ката́лась · оно ката́лось · они ката́лись. — Wiktionary, «кататься» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Мне нравится кататься на лыжах, на коньках, на велосипеде и на лодке. — I like to ski, skate, cycle, and row.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.prompt: I dragged the heavy baggage to the airport.
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Собака ___ (гнаться — to drive, chase (oneself)) за кошкой.
exercises.why: **гналась** is the past tense (feminine) of **гнаться** (to chase, to pursue [with за (za, + accusative) ‘someone’]) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **гоняться** for many directions. past: он гна́лся, гнался́ · она гнала́сь · оно гнало́сь, гна́лось · они гнали́сь, гна́лись. — Wiktionary, «гнаться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: The dog ran after the cat.
exercises.context: Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Мы ___ (плыть — to swim, float, sail, one way) против ветра.
exercises.why: **плыли** is the past tense (plural) of **плыть** (to swim, to float) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **плавать** for many directions. past: он плы́л · она плыла́ · оно плы́ло, плыло́ · они плы́ли. — Wiktionary, «плыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verb плавать — плыть, поплыть belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить — идти, пойти; "плавать" (like "ходить") is a "repeated function" verb. Note the ways in which it is used: Я умею плавать. — I know how to swim. Дерево плавает в воде. — Wood floats in water. Я плаваю на этом корабле. — I sail (work) on this ship. In naval terminology the verb "идти" instead of "плыть" is commonly used: Я иду на этом корабле. Наш корабль идёт по Чёрному морю. Мы шли в Архангельск.» — DLI, Lesson 73.  Compare: «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: За Томом ___ (гоняться — to drive, chase (oneself)) папарацци.

exercises.q: Не мешайся, не ___ (лезть — to climb, one way) не в своё дело!
exercises.why: **лезь** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **лезть** (to climb (up, on to), to scramble) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **лазить** for many directions. imperative: ле́зь · ле́зьте. — Wiktionary, «лезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite).» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: По дороге ___ (нестись — to carry on foot (oneself)) грузовик.
exercises.why: **нёсся** is the past tense (masculine) of **нестись** (to hurtle, to dash, to race, to tear, to scurry (to move rapidly, violently, or without control)) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **носиться** for many directions. past: он нёсся · она несла́сь · оно несло́сь · они несли́сь. — Wiktionary, «нестись» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Researchers have also included the reflexive verbs катиться/кататься, гнаться/гоняться, нестись/носиться, and тащиться/таскаться.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
